title: AnswerBlock
description: GENUI-01: one typed, renderable part of an answer, defined once here. A package returns blocks on `PluginResult.blocks`; the hub validates them, applies the output floor to each string by band, streams each as a `block` turn-stream event and stores them on the turn's `blocks`. Every client renders the same record: the web kit dispatches `kind` to the Element of the same name, Go renders it natively, the robot says `alt` when it has no screen. A client that does not know a `kind` falls back to `alt`. Envelope: `id`, `kind`, `schema_version`, `producer` (package id), `alt` (one plain sentence a screen reader, a TV fallback or the robot can say), optional `min_band`, `provenance`, `created_at`, `hlc` (the clock stamp every synced record carries) and `after_paragraph` (hub-stamped placement in the reply text), and the kind's `props`. Each kind's `props` mirror the props of the kit Element of the same name, so the web render is a pass-through; render-only Element props (visible counts, animation flags, callbacks, nodes) are not part of the record. Prop names are the Element's own (camelCase). Flat, never recursive: no block holds another block. The v1 kinds are a closed, additive list; a later kind is a new enum value and a new `props` shape, never a change to an existing one.

kind.description: The v1 answer-block kinds. Closed and additive: a later kind (series_chart, stat, split_bar, media_list, place_cards, map, swatches, tabs, filter_chips, calculator) lands with its kit Element and is appended here.

block_id.description: Stable identity of this block. Unique within a turn's block list.

producer.description: The id of the package that returned the block.

alt.description: One plain sentence that says what the block shows, for a screen reader, a client with no renderer for this kind, or the robot's voice.

min_band.description: Optional. The youngest age band that may be shown this block; absent means every band. The output floor still applies to each string.

provenance.description: Free-text provenance for the block, such as the producing call or the data it was built from (the same shape TurnArtifact uses).

hlc.description: Hybrid logical clock: wall_ms:counter:node (7.3), the same shape every other synced record type uses.

after_paragraph.description: GENUI-13a: where the block sits in the released reply text, the same meaning as `AnswerImageSet.after_paragraph`: how many paragraphs of released text come before it. 0 is before any text; absent means after the whole reply, so a record written before this field renders as it always did. Stamped by the hub only (a package returns blocks before any prose exists and never sets it; the host drops a value a package sends). Paragraphs are counted and split by `paragraphCount` and `splitAfterParagraph` in `spec/interpreters` (TS and Python), so the hub and every client count alike. Placement is by readiness and paragraph boundary, never by matching the block's words to the prose.

id.description: The key of this column's value in each row.

formats.description: Per-column formats by column id, for a column that carries no `format` of its own.

relativeTo.description: Epoch milliseconds that relative dates are measured from, so every client renders the same words.

cell.description: One table cell: plain data, never markup.

src.description: A picture reference. The hub rewrites it to a hub-proxied id before the block is streamed or stored; a package never sends a client a third-party image address.

traits.description: One entry per trait label, in order: the option's value for that trait, or false when it lacks the trait.

recommendedId.description: The id of the option marked as the pick. Absent: no option is marked.

place.description: The place label, shown small caps on the hero.

unit.description: The unit of every temperature in the block.

moon.description: The moon's phase for a night card. Absent: the card keeps its generic moon.

advice.description: Advice chips drawn under the current conditions. Absent or empty: none.

icon.description: A kit icon name. An unknown name draws no icon.

alert.description: A weather alert banner drawn above the hero. Absent: none.

news_story_card.description: One story as a card draws it (NEWS-00). Every string passed the viewer's band floor on the hub before it got here. `image` holds same-origin hub paths, never the publisher's address. `open_url` is absent for a child and for any viewer whose band may not follow outbound links.

sourceIconUrl.description: Hub-relative favicon route for the story's source.

outlets.description: How many publishers cover this story.

focal.description: Where the picture's subject sits, worked out once on the hub: x and y are percentages of the image, aspect is its width over its height. A client crops around this point and never analyses the picture itself.

opened.description: The viewer opened this story before; the card dims.

group.description: The day group a row belongs to, named by the hub ("This morning"). Consecutive rows with the same group draw under one heading.

kicker.description: The hub-built line above the headline ("Top story · 4 outlets", "Science"). It passed the viewer's band floor like every other string.

section_style.description: NEWS-SECTION-STYLES-01. The arrangement of a channel page, from the topic's section_style in spec/news/topics.json. Read only when layout is channel and ignored for any other layout. Absent draws the lead-and-list page.

dateline.description: The line under the title ("Sat, Oct 17 · Updated 7:40").

filters.description: One row of topic chips under the header. An empty `id` means All. The page's `filter` action carries the chosen `filter_id`.

focal.description: Where the picture's subject sits, worked out once on the hub: x and y are percentages of the image, aspect is its width over its height. A client crops around this point and never analyses the picture itself.

speech.description: What Listen speaks, in order; the hub builds it from strings that passed the viewer's floor, so the client never assembles speech from other fields.

article_block.description: NEWS-00: one block of a cleaned article, defined once here so the hub, the web kit and Go render the same list. The closed model the one reader (`extractFullArticle`) returns: headings with ids, paragraphs of inline runs, lists, label and value rows, tables, figures, notes and quotes. Links: `target` names a book page on the reference reader; `href` is an outbound address and appears only in a teen or adult copy (the hub removes it for a child, who gets plain text). Additive after the first release: a new block type is a new `oneOf` member.

href.description: An outbound address. Present only when the viewer's band may follow outbound links.

article_inline.description: One run of text inside a paragraph, list item or quote.

src.description: A same-origin hub path, never the publisher's address.
Hub cache image reference only; never a remote URL.
